skill.name: threejs-geometry
skill.description: Creating and shaping three.js geometry: built-in shapes, 3D text, vertex buffers and attributes, merging, instancing, batching, point clouds and lines, on WebGL or with WebGPU and TSL. Use when building 3D shapes or text, custom vertex data, custom meshes, instanced meshes, or point clouds.
skill.summary: Build and optimize Three.js geometry with reference examples for vertex buffers, instancing, batching, and WebGPU.
skill.author: cloudai-x

content.value_statement: Three.js geometry work requires careful choices about vertex data, draw calls, and renderer compatibility. This skill provides focused examples for shapes, custom buffers, instancing, and WebGPU adaptations.
actual_capabilities: Provides examples for built-in shapes, path-based geometry, and extruded text with a loaded font.
Explains indexed BufferGeometry, typed attributes, normalized colors, interleaved buffers, and vertex updates.
Demonstrates InstancedMesh transforms, instance colors, runtime updates, and instance identification through raycasting.
Shows BatchedMesh setup, geometry merging, vertex welding, tangent generation, and graphics resource disposal.
Covers point clouds, line primitives, edge rendering, geometry transforms, and morph targets.
Documents WebGPU renderer differences and TSL examples for sprite-based points and per-instance displacement.
limitations: The reference targets Three.js r186; other releases can require API changes.
The package contains one instructional Markdown file, not a runnable application or automated test suite.
Examples require a configured Three.js environment; the text example also requires a separately supplied font asset.
Rendering behavior and draw-call savings depend on the backend, browser, hardware, and scene structure.

use_cases.title: Prototype Interactive 3D Shapes
use_cases.description: Choose built-in or path-based geometry and add text, edges, and wireframes to a browser scene.

use_cases.title: Optimize Repeated Scene Objects
use_cases.description: Compare instancing, batching, and static merging while managing transforms, colors, bounds, and shared resources.

use_cases.title: Adapt Visualizations for WebGPU
use_cases.description: Replace unsupported line loops, adapt point sizing, and express per-instance offsets with TSL nodes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Shape
prompt_templates.prompt: Use threejs-geometry to create a rotating box in Three.js r186 with WebGLRenderer and MeshNormalMaterial. Include scene, camera, and render-loop setup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start a minimal geometry scene.

prompt_templates.title: Build Custom Vertex Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an indexed quad using BufferGeometry with positions, normals, UVs, and normalized byte colors. Explain attribute sizes and updating one vertex safely.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: define and update custom geometry.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Repeated Meshes
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace 1,000 identical box meshes with InstancedMesh, preserving transforms and colors. Include runtime updates, bounds refresh, raycast instance identification, and shared-resource disposal guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reduce repeated mesh draw calls.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Scene for WebGPU
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt a Three.js r186 scene with large points, closed lines, and custom instance offsets for WebGPURenderer. Use sprite-based points, repeated endpoints, and TSL positionLocal.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: address renderer compatibility and custom instance data.

output_examples.input: How should I render 1,000 colored boxes efficiently?
output: Use InstancedMesh when all boxes share geometry and a compatible material.
Assign each transform and color, then mark the instance matrix and color buffers for upload.
Refresh bounding volumes after movement and use the raycast instance identifier to select individual boxes.

output_examples.input: My large points and closed line disappear or look different under WebGPU. What should change?
output: The WebGPU backend renders point primitives at one pixel regardless of material size.
Use an instanced Sprite with PointsNodeMaterial for larger points.
Replace LineLoop with Line and repeat the first point at the end to close the shape.

output_examples.input: What must I update after changing vertex positions?
output: Mark the position attribute for upload after editing its values.
Recompute vertex normals when the surface shape changes.
Refresh the bounding box and bounding sphere for culling and raycasting.

best_practices: Confirm your Three.js version and renderer backend before applying examples, especially for WebGPU-specific behavior.
Match attribute layouts and index state before merging or batching geometries; refresh bounds after geometry or instance movement.
Share geometry deliberately, choose segment counts carefully, and dispose resources only when their users no longer need them.
anti_patterns: Creating separate draw calls for thousands of identical meshes without considering InstancedMesh.
Editing vertex or instance data without upload flags or refreshed bounding volumes.
Assuming WebGL point sizes, line loops, or ShaderMaterial code transfer unchanged to WebGPURenderer.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides a Three.js geometry reference with JavaScript examples for shapes, custom buffers, instancing, batching, morph targets, and renderer differences.

faq.question: Which Three.js version does it target?
faq.answer: The source targets Three.js r186. Check API compatibility before using its examples with another release.

faq.question: Does it cover both WebGL and WebGPU?
faq.answer: Yes. Most examples use WebGLRenderer, while a dedicated section explains WebGPURenderer differences and TSL adaptations.

faq.question: Does the package include a runnable application or font files?
faq.answer: No. It contains one Markdown reference file. Configure Three.js separately and supply the font asset required by the text example.

faq.question: When should I use instancing instead of batching?
faq.answer: Use InstancedMesh for repeated copies of one geometry. BatchedMesh supports different geometries sharing a material, with performance depending on the rendering backend.

faq.question: Can I use this skill with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools. State your Three.js version and renderer when requesting geometry changes.
